agent.problem: Six of the eight choice cards are multiple choice: cards 2, 4, 7, 8, 13 and 15. With only one true-or-false card and one fill-in-the-blank card, multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

agent.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the reaction "Yep.", the statement that Jeroboam does evil, and the sentence about restoring Israel's borders.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: The setup asks which prophet was sent to Nineveh but cites "Jonah 1:1-2". That citation supplies the name Jonah, immediately identifying "Jonah son of Amittai" and ruling out the other two answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

agent.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Back up north.", the sentence introducing Zechariah's reign, and "Friend, don't get too attached to this one." It is not the walkthrough's opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: The earlier cards only indicate that Zechariah's reign will be short. They give no basis for choosing "months" rather than "weeks" or "years", so the blank depends on luck rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: "Six months.", the sentence about Zechariah's evil, and the sentence introducing Shallum's conspiracy.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker derive how many generations the LORD promised Jehu. The setup does not provide a way to reason from "four", "three" or "seven"; it only asks for an unseen number.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: Four of the six choice cards depend on luck or prior Bible knowledge rather than the earlier cards: card 2 asks for the officer's name, card 4 for Pekah's exact reign length, card 6 for the captured people's fate, and card 10 for the gate's name. Only the conspiracy pattern in card 7 and the LORD's activity in card 11 offer a reasonable basis for an informed pick, so most choices in this stop are not informed guesses.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: The earlier cards give no clue to the gate's name. A baker cannot reason out "Upper" rather than "Horse" or "Fish" from the statement that Jotham rebuilt a gate, so this blank tests unseen wording rather than reasoned meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
